implementationScope: package-only progressive JFIF 4:2:0 incremental session with semantic-unit transport, dynamic pre-SOF table ownership, SOF DQT ownership transfer, first-SOS DQT release, actual-only coefficient planes, exact current Huffman payloads, render-only quantization widening and validated-EOI final-ready compaction

cases.mechanismPressure: all ten scan previews exercise smoothing and ISLOW IDCT after persistent bound quantization storage is narrowed to UInt8; one render-only UInt16[64] scratch is reused for per-block widening
large final-only raster proves 192 bytes of persistent quantization width are removed while the additional 128-byte render widening table composes with row, IDCT and smoothing scratch
restart-heavy entropy suspension remains unchanged while final raster uses the render-only widening table and releases it at EOI compaction

requiredInvariants: All v12 transport, dynamic pre-frame ownership, SOF DQT transfer, source semantics, actual coefficient geometry, dynamic Huffman, preview backing, restart and EOI-compaction invariants remain unchanged.
Progressive DQT parsing accepts only precision zero and nonzero 8-bit values, so a bound component quantization value is exactly representable in one byte throughout its cross-scan lifetime.
Persistent base fixed state is exactly 384 bytes: three 64-byte natural-order bound quantization tables plus three 64-byte progression arrays.
Render fixed scratch is exactly 512 bytes: 256-byte ISLOW workspace, 128-byte smoothing coefficient scratch and one 128-byte UInt16 quantization widening table.
Before each block IDCT, the selected persistent UInt8 quantization table is widened into the single render-only UInt16[64] table. The shared JPEGISlowIDCT API and arithmetic contract are unchanged.

Block smoothing reads the same persistent UInt8 quantization values as integers. Because all accepted values are 1 through 255, this changes storage width only, not smoothing arithmetic or source semantics.

Compared with v12, persistent state decreases by 192 bytes and render scratch increases by 128 bytes. A render-dominated operation peak therefore decreases by exactly 64 bytes; entropy-only phases gain the full 192-byte persistent reduction.

The tiny source has persistentBaseStateBytes 1664, maximum persistentStateBytes 3840, renderScratchBytes 2880 and totalStateBytes 6720. Its final-ready retained value remains 897 bytes, maximum retained authority is 5151 bytes and operation peak is 8031 bytes.
The 576x576 source has maximum retained authority 998302 bytes, final-ready retained 995328 bytes and operation peak 2010846 bytes.
The restart64 source has maximum retained authority 15262 bytes, final-ready retained 12288 bytes and operation peak 30430 bytes.

Pre-frame and frame-q high-water remain 128 bytes for all retained sources; final/high-water DHT values remain 90/95, 98/169 and 89/135 bytes. The quantization-width change must not perturb any earlier authority or entropy state.

This profile does not qualify malloc headers, allocator size classes, Swift object/pointer fields, physical RSS, non-JFIF semantics, embedded ICC, other sampling modes or perceptual reconstruction quality.
